rows: How many times do we have to be ready before someone lets us begin?
Brawling is a question nobody asks properly. Who decides when the fight starts?
Danger is a question with a price on it. Who pays it?
Pace is a question of who is allowed to set it. Are you letting me?
The people are asking the same question I am. Will this be a real contest?
I have been asking for a fair start for a while, and I am still asking.
Am I on this card because I earned it, or because I was let in?
Who decided the stance was wrong? Is it so strange that I want to be seen standing straight?
Technique, according to whom? Who taught you that the standard is yours alone?
Strikes first, then what? Who decides whether that is enough?
A gamble you did not choose is a question someone else answers. Who answers yours?
A stall is a question you do not want asked. Shall I ask it?
The people deserve a contest where both sides are heard. Will you hear me?
You think you are among the best. Who measured that, and who let you measure it?
Who taught you to be proud of your {strength}? Is that pride earned, or handed to you?
I have wondered about your {strength}. Would you let me test it fairly?
Cool head: does that count for anything? Okay. Does calm make you right, or only quiet?
Does that land with you? Can we agree on that without someone talking over us?
Could I ask you a question about that? I would like an honest answer.
Who keeps the count? Who keeps the count? Can we agree on it first?
On the mat, when will you let me take a breath? Or will you keep talking over me?
Grounded or standing, who gets to decide the next move?
Will you face me? Will you let me finish a sentence?
Is that a proper answer? Is that one you believe, or one you are repeating?
Will you let the question stand? Will you, or will you talk over me again?
Does that land with you? Is that what you meant?
Can I accept that? Will you hold to it when the bell goes?
I will wrestle this match, and I will ask my questions in the ring.
Will you let me be patient? I want a fair start, and I will make sure I get one.
Whatever happens, will the people see what happened?
Is this finished? I do not think it is.
I have one question left, and you will answer it when the bell goes.
Would you accept a charge without an example? Neither should I. I cannot give you one that proves it.
Can I actually show you what I meant? No, not with enough certainty. Let me take that back.
Can we leave the charge there, then? I'd rather we found out what happens at the bell.
That's a fair answer. Can we agree to judge the wrestling itself?
Why not give both of us a fair chance to demonstrate what we can do? The people can judge the result.
Who earns the fall when we are both given the same opportunity? That is the question worth answering.
Who gets to judge what happens in the ring, if not the people watching?
Set the accusation aside. What can we both demonstrate if we are given a fair contest?
You have told everyone how you intend to answer my {strength}. Will you give me a fair chance to test that answer?
Who decides that your answer to my {strength} works? Let us give the people a contest and find out.
Yes, that is fair to both of us. Let the people judge what we can actually demonstrate.
I accept that standard. Nobody should have to defend an allegation without something behind it.
Who decided how many years a wrestler needs before they deserve an equal chance? Let's settle it here.
Your experience deserves respect. Why should it decide the contest before either of us gets to wrestle?
What have the years taught me? To ask what happens next before I give away the position.
Experience is useful when it gives you another answer, not when it stops you listening to the question.
You have studied me. Have you asked what happens when I refuse the position you prepared for?
Who decided the notes you took on me are more important than the choices I make tonight?
Studying a match means asking why a position worked, not just remembering the move that followed.
I prepare for what you might do, then ask what the actual contest requires. Isn't that the point?
